title: Simulation of an input-word equality test
statement: Let $A$ be a map from labels to register-program instructions, with initial label $l_0$, and let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to each decider and bit string. Suppose $x$ is a bit string of the form $\langle 1^n,w\rangle$, where $w$ is canonical, and $A(l)$ tests whether register $r$ equals the input payload, with successor labels $l_1$ for equality and $l_0'$ otherwise. For any register valuation $v$, output word, and integer $W$ such that the length of the binary expansion of $v(r)$ is at most $W$, the compiled program simulates this instruction from the configuration with label $l$, valuation $v$, and the given output to the configuration with the same valuation and output, and label $l_1$ precisely when the binary expansion of $v(r)$ equals $w$ (and $l_0'$ otherwise); at every step before the endpoint, no oracle call is pending and every work-tape head position lies between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: An instruction map and initial label
An oracle assigning Boolean answers by decider and bit string
Input is a valid plain encoding with canonical payload
Register r and instruction testing equality with the input payload
Binary expansion length of v(r) is at most W
